cases.description: Verify that getUnstableBars() always returns 0 for a freshly instantiated CashFlow implementation. Since the method contains no conditional logic, the only expected behavior is to return the constant value 0.
Call getUnstableBars() multiple times on the same CashFlow instance to ensure the method is idempotent and consistently returns 0 regardless of any prior interactions with the object.
Create two independent CashFlow objects and verify each returns 0, confirming that the method does not rely on any shared mutable state.
Invoke getValue(index) on a valid index before calling getUnstableBars() to ensure prior instance method calls do not affect the returned constant.
Call the static addCost(rawPrice, holdingCost, true) utility method with arbitrary arguments before calling getUnstableBars() to confirm static helpers have no side‑effects on the instance.
Execute getUnstableBars() simultaneously from multiple threads on the same CashFlow instance and verify each thread receives 0, demonstrating thread‑safety of the method.
Attempt to call getValue() with an out‑of‑range index, catch the resulting exception, then call getUnstableBars() and verify it still returns 0, showing the method is unaffected by prior failures.
